subject: Post-demo: Dedicated SLO & hardware tradeoffs for Ember Health
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo: Dedicated SLO & hardware tradeoffs for Ember Health

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and some concrete next steps so we can size a Dedicated validation that matches Ember's production SLOs. I pulled our notes from the call; if I missed or mis-specified anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Summary of requirements (from today):
- Latency target: 95th percentile <= 150ms for single-turn generation when streaming partial tokens to the client (critical for UX).
- Throughput: steady-state ~100 requests/minute; peak bursts up to ~450 reqs/min (short windows, 3–5 minutes).
- Concurrency: typical concurrency 6–10 simultaneous sessions; internal load test should validate up to 16 concurrent workers.
- Average prompt length: ~160 tokens; expected response length ~120 tokens (with occasional longer summaries up to 600 tokens).
- Streaming: required (server-side partial token streaming to browser/player).
- Model preference: open to 70B dense vs a 70B quantized 4-bit variant depending on cost/latency tradeoffs.

Initial hardware tradeoffs we discussed:
- H100 80GB: best single-request latency for large models, strong for batching+KV cache, higher hourly cost.
- A100 80GB: solid latency, slightly cheaper than H100 in many clouds; kernel maturity is very good on our runtime.
- L40S / RTX-class: good for cost-conscious throughput if you accept higher tail latency on very large context windows.

Attachments: perf_matrix.csv (synthetic microbenchmarks we ran on similar models).

Proposal (next steps):
1) Redwood runs a 48-hour Dedicated validation using Ember's representative prompt set (you provide a small anonymized sample). We’ll run both H100 and A100 profiles and return an apples-to-apples perf + cost report.
2) We'll instrument the run for streaming latency (1ms sampling resolution), concurrency scaling, and prefix/KV cache hit-rate.
3) We propose two reserved capacity profiles (low-latency C1 / cost-optimized C2). I’ll attach a quick sizing sketch after you confirm the sample dataset.

Can you: (a) share a 1,000-row sample of typical prompts (anonymized) via the Drive link or secure upload, and (b) confirm the procurement timeline (are you aiming to finalize an arrangement by end-of-June)?

If that works, I’ll loop in our infra lead (Karthik) and Vanessa (solutions) to schedule the validation window and scope.

Thanks —
Vivek Kulkarni

Vivek —

Appreciate the clear summary. Confirming a few items from our side:
- The 95p <= 150ms is accurate and non-negotiable for the clinician-facing workflow. For background-batch jobs we can tolerate higher latency but those are not on the critical path.
- Bursts: the 400–500/min bursts are realistic around shift-changes; typically these last 2–6 minutes.
- Tokens: the 600-token long responses are rare but important for case summaries — if that materially changes GPU selection let us know.

I uploaded a 1,000-row anonymized prompt sample to the shared Drive folder (link same as above). Also attaching our SLA_requirements.pdf — it has the procurement standard SLO language and an internal cost target band.

Procurement timeline: target decision by 30 June 2027; legal review and SOC 2 evidence are gating items (we’ll send SOC 2 info requests separately). We may ask for a brief proof-of-concept purchase order to get a validation cluster on our account for a short term.

Two quick questions:
1) For streaming measurements, do you simulate browser RTTs and chunked responses, or are those measured end-to-end from our hosted client?
2) Will the Reserved profiles include GPU-hour burn rate estimates and a per-token cost projection?

Thanks —

Alex —

Great, received the sample and the SLA doc — thanks. Quick answers to your questions and an outline of the validation plan.

Streaming measurements
- We'll run two types of measurements: (1) server-side instrumentation that reports token emission time deltas (the streaming chunk times) to reproduce what Ember’s browser would observe; (2) an end-to-end synthetic client that emulates browser RTT and chunk assembly so we can account for network jitter. Both sets are included in the validation report.

Reserved profiles & cost projections
- Yes — the reserved profiles will include estimated GPU-hour burn and a projected per-1k-token cost based on measured throughput, batching, and cache hit rates. See attached reserved_profiles.xlsx for the preliminary numbers.

Sizing sketch (high level) — two candidate profiles:
- Profile C1 (latency-first, conservative): 2x H100 80GB with autoscale cushion (expected 95p latency <= 140ms for 70B quantized 4-bit with streaming enabled). Reserved throughput: ~800 tokens/sec sustained, supports peaks described. Estimated monthly reserved cost: ~$85k (cloud variability applies).
- Profile C2 (cost-first): 4x A100 80GB (smaller per-GPU cost but slightly higher tail latency on long contexts). Expected 95p latency <= 180ms for same model/config; reserved throughput ~750 tokens/sec. Estimated monthly reserved cost: ~$58k.

Validation plan
1) Redwood provisions a short-lived Dedicated cluster in your account/tenant (we can work with procurement on a PoC PO).
2) We ingest your 1k sample and run 24–48 hour replay at scaled rates (steady-state + peak bursts).
3) Deliverables: per-profile perf sheets, per-token cost, KV cache hit-rate analysis, streaming latency distribution (P50/P90/P95/P99), and an ops runbook for production rollout.

Operational caveats and tradeoffs
- For very long responses (400–600 tokens), we expect increased tail latency on A100 configs; H100 shows better tail behavior because of better transformer kernel latency at long sequence lengths.
- If Ember wants to optimize cost further, we can explore mixed fleets (H100 for low-latency endpoints + A100 for background/summary jobs) with automatic routing.

Next steps:
- Can Karthik coordinate with your infra/procurement to set up the Proof-of-Concept cluster (we’ll provide a short checklist)?
- Proposed validation window: May 17–19 (we can also do May 24–26 if procurement needs more time).

If that all looks good I’ll schedule the cluster provisioning and loop in infra/ops for the runbook.

Thanks —
Vivek
